## Security fixes

- **A failed reload kept serving the old tool list (fail-open).** When the tool list couldn't be rebuilt after a config change, for example because two servers claimed the same tool name, the gateway kept the previous list, so a tool you had just revoked stayed callable. Now a failed rebuild serves no server tools until the config resolves again. The five `gateway__` verbs stay up, and the failure is in the audit log.
- **Server credentials could follow a redirect to another origin.** A server's static headers, bearer token or OAuth token went along when the server redirected the gateway elsewhere, including from https to plain http. Credentials now go only to the configured scheme, host and port, and a redirect to any other origin is refused. For SSE servers, the gateway sends nothing to another origin, whatever address the server's endpoint event names.

## Other fixes

- Writers no longer lose each other's changes. Every write to `toolhost.json` or the request queue takes a lock, and a save from a stale read is refused (`config changed on disk since it was read — nothing written`) instead of undoing a newer change, such as bringing back a tool you revoked. The request queue is written atomically.
- `gateway__enable` refuses an unapproved tool even when the config has no `enabled` list.
- A denial with an empty reason is still shown to the agent.
- Names from a `passthrough` upstream are checked against the tool-name rules.
- `toolhost requests` shows everything a server petition carries: the URL, the command and every argument, quoted. Control characters in text from the agent are quoted too. A petition carrying both a URL and a command can't be accepted.
- A direct call to a tool that isn't on the list is recorded in the audit log as `tool_forbidden`, with the name capped at 256 bytes.
- Changing `call_timeout` while calls are in flight no longer races them.
- A missing OAuth grant now points at the command that exists, `toolhost mcp auth <name>`.
- `toolhost help` no longer prints a group without a title.

## Protocol

- A request whose `Origin` header isn't a local origin gets `403` before the key is checked, on every route, as the MCP transport specification requires. A `Host` header that isn't local, on a loopback connection, gets `403` on every route, not only `/mcp`.

## Changes you might notice

- A redirect that changes scheme, host or port, including http to https, is refused. Configure the server's final URL.
- Write locks live in `~/.toolhost/locks/`.
- Homebrew installs a cask: `brew install gettoolhost/tap/toolhost`. The formula is gone.

## Also since v0.0.3

- `toolhost attach` for 12 clients, merging one `local-gateway` entry and leaving every other entry alone; `--project`, `--stdio`, `--dry-run` and `--print`.
- The five `gateway__` verbs (`discover`, `enable`, `disable`, `call`, `request`) and the request queue you answer with `toolhost requests`.
- `toolhost mcp`: add, list, get, remove, enable, disable, test, tools, auth, logout and import.
- Config and state under `~/.toolhost`, a private environment per folder, and `toolhost init --shared` for a committable one.

## Verify the download

```bash
cosign verify-blob --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/gettoolhost/toolhost-local/.github/workflows/release.yml@.*' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  checksums.txt
sha256sum -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing
gh attestation verify toolhost_darwin_arm64.tar.gz -R gettoolhost/toolhost-local
```
